purpose: revise the MEE scientific surface so that ODSP is presented as ecological-state distribution prediction across validated state-space geometries, using the machine-checked common held-out log-score gain from n2-state-space-generality-v1, without changing any frozen empirical endpoint
title: State-resolved ecological prediction: from flat suitability to transferable ecological-state distributions
common_prediction_target: q(A|X) on a scientifically declared ecological state space
required_manuscript_changes: Abstract and Introduction define a distributional target q(A|X) rather than restricting the framework to finite categorical P(A|X)
Methods distinguish probability mass from continuous, circular and joint densities and require richer and baseline scores to use the same reference measure
Methods state that the learner, lower-information comparator and independent validation unit remain explicit scientific design choices
Methods retain finite-discrete entropy, effective-state count, Brier score and top-1 metrics as state-space-specific rather than universal quantities
Results report the cross-geometry 10-of-10 benchmark and its maximum numerical error separately from the older 1873 finite-discrete representation obligations
Discussion distinguishes state-space estimand generality from biological generality and from finite-discrete information-theoretic summaries
The joint continuous-circular coupling gain is described only as directional predictive information and not as a causal or symmetric interaction
